title: Rejection record
description: What an agent writes down when a step is rejected or fails. A record that says only "error" tells the next reader nothing, and the next reader is usually a retry loop. Every field here exists so that the next decision, by a machine or a person, starts from what is already known.

record_id.description: Unique across the task. Two attempts never share one.

attempt.description: Which record this is for the task, counting from one. It counts records, not retries: a record is written on every rejection or failure, including the ones that end the task.

stage.description: Where in the workflow it happened, in the workflow's own words. "evidence.receipt", "action.refund". Not which function threw.

failure_class.description: What happened. This is the field that decides the response. escalate and stop are not classes; they are next steps, and a task can escalate for any of the five reasons.

reason.description: One sentence a person can read. Never a stack trace and never the word error on its own.

required_by.description: The rule or step that needs it. So the reader can tell a hard requirement from a preference.

how_to_obtain.description: The concrete next action. "Ask the requester to upload the receipt", not "obtain evidence".

side_effects.description: Every action this task may have taken outside itself. Empty is a claim that nothing outside the system was touched, and it is a claim the writer is responsible for.

idempotency_key.description: The only handle on the specific thing that might have run. Without it there is nothing to reconcile against.

state.description: Never a guess. A timeout is unknown until a status query says otherwise.

max_attempts.description: The task's total, shared by every layer. Not this layer's own count.

what_changes_next_attempt.description: Required whenever another attempt is planned. A retry with nothing written here is a retry nobody can justify.

deadline.description: An absolute instant, not a countdown. A record read an hour later should say when the task was due.

owner.description: Who is accountable for the next step. A queue is not an owner. A team name is not an owner. A role that a specific person holds today is.

respond_by.description: When somebody must have looked at this. Absolute, like deadline.

allOf.$comment: An uncertain action must not be re-issued until reconciliation completes, and the record has to say so in words a retry loop cannot misread. It also has to name the action that may have run.
If another attempt is planned, the record must say what will be different about it.
An escalation with no queue and no response time is work sent nowhere.
A missing_evidence record that names nothing missing cannot be acted on.
A policy conflict is a disagreement between the plan and confirmed state, so the state has to be in the record.
